name: Warli
fonts: Fraunces display · a geometric sans for the figures
history: Before: women painted white rice-paste figures onto red-ochre mud walls for weddings and harvest — among India's oldest unbroken wall traditions. After: moved from wall to paper and canvas in the 1970s (Jivya Soma Mashe), now a GI-tagged global style.
ideas: Design idea: extreme restraint — one ink, one ground. Triangle-torso figures = a tiny icon grammar. Proof that a two-token palette can carry an entire world.

name: Gond
tagline: line, dot & dash — the forest breathing
fonts: Rozha One display · Karla for captions
history: Before: digna and bhittichitra — ritual mud-wall and floor art of the Pardhan Gond, in pigment from charcoal, soil, sap and dung. After: Jangarh Singh Shyam turned it into studio painting in 1980s Bhopal; 'Jangarh Kalam' is now a named school.
ideas: Design idea: every surface fills with a signature of dots and dashes — a texture token. A vivid multi-hue palette, yet unified by that single fill rhythm.

name: Mithila
tagline: the double line that never leaves a gap
history: Before: women of Mithila painted kohbar wedding-chamber walls for centuries, filling every space with nature and deity. After: the 1934 drought and later paper commissions moved it to handmade sheets; now one of India's most recognised folk forms.
ideas: Design idea: horror vacui as a layout rule — no empty space, a double outline on every shape, and bold fields of saturated natural dye.

name: Pattachitra
fonts: Fraunces · Noto Oriya for the caption line
history: Before: temple-town painters made pattachitra — cloth scrolls of Jagannath and the epics — in mineral and shell pigments, bound to the Puri temple's ritual calendar. After: Raghurajpur became a living heritage craft village; the form now travels as fine art.
ideas: Design idea: a strict iconographic grammar — ornate borders, flat figures, no shadow. Everything is outline and fill, like a hand-inked icon set.

name: Bhil
history: Before: the Bhil — one of India's largest Adivasi nations — marked walls with pithora ritual horses and deities for vows and harvest. After: Lado Bai, Bhuri Bai and others brought it to canvas from the 1980s Bharat Bhavan circle.
ideas: Design idea: fields built entirely from dots — a pointillist fill token. The dots carry colour and texture at once; the figure is the negative space between them.

name: Saura / Santal
tagline: the icon-mural, and a script made on purpose
fonts: Fraunces · Noto Ol Chiki — a native tribal script
history: Before: Saura idital wall-icons honoured ancestors in white on red-ochre — and the Munda languages had no script of their own. After: Raghunath Murmu devised Ol Chiki for Santali in 1925; it is now official and in Unicode — the art's missing alphabet, finally written.
ideas: Design idea: a whole mural as one framed icon, figures woven into a border like a single glyph. The real lesson: a design system can include inventing the writing itself.
